newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina compensates relatives of dirty war victims.
newsitem.headline: Argentina compensates relatives of dirty war victims.

text.p: The Argentine government authorised compensation on Wednesday for the first group of relatives of those who vanished during the military regime's "dirty war" against suspected leftists.
Each of the 50 relatives of "disappeared" Argentines will receive $200,000 in government bonds starting next year, Interior Minister Carlos Corach said at the signing ceremony.

"This is an historic event," Corach, quoted by the state news agency Telam, told a group of relatives who attended the ceremony. "It will not return the lives of your relatives, but it is a small compensation society owes you."

A spokeswoman for the Relatives of Detained and Disappeared human-rights group welcomed the move but said it will not stop them from demanding a full explanation of the fate of the victims. Up to 30,000 people disappeared during the 1976-83 "dirty war" on suspected leftists.
"This is a political admission that they have been abducted and assassinated, but all the gold in the world cannot pay for their lives," Lilia Orfano, who lost two children, told Reuters.
"And we will keep fighting for an answer to what they have done to all our relatives."
Some 7,000 people have presented claims under a 1992 law providing for compensation to the victims' families.
The military junta members were tried and handed long prison sentences after the country returned to democratic rule. But President Carlos Menem pardoned them soon after taking office in 1989.
